items.title: Inventory every count-claim guard that actually binds at HEAD, as a rerunnable tool
items.acceptance: An executable at tools/guard-inventory.mjs re-derives, from the repo at run time (never from hardcoded literals), a table of every guard in test/ whose subject is a numeric or structural COUNT claim about a document: for each one it names the file, the test title, the document claim it reads, where the expected value comes from (derived from src/corpus.js at test time vs. a literal written into the test file), and whether any guard asserts a floor on the SIZE of the suite itself. It also emits the current test-file line count per file and the total. The output must explicitly record the verdict on the inherited '>= 121 tests' floor premise: present or absent, with the evidence that settles it.
items.notes: PLAN confirmed by reading that NO literal suite-size floor exists in test/ — '121' occurs only in two prose comments in readme-matrix-consistency.test.js, and .github/workflows/test.yml carries an explicit written refusal to add a count assertion. So S-1's 'retire the COUNT floor' half likely has nothing to retire and W-2 is net-NEW tooling, not a replacement. The tool must SAY that rather than manufacture a floor to retire. Measured start: 129 tests across 7 files (readme-tags 31, args 28, cli 29, select 18, pipe 16, readme-matrix-consistency 5, node-support-citation 2); test/ 4,587 lines; src+bin 594. tools/ is outside the cited pathspec so creating it cannot falsify the README citation. Floor verdict ABSENT was re-derived INDEPENDENTLY by the conductor (own grep: only 3+-digit literals in assertion position across test/ are the seeds 12345 and 99999; 121 occurs only in two comments in readme-matrix-consistency.test.js). Non-hardcoding proved by DISCRIMINATOR: on a mutated scratch tree with one extra test file the tool moved 4587->4591 lines, 129->131 runner tests, 93->94 excluded, and self-flagged a static-vs-runner DISAGREE rather than smoothing it. Two classifications spot-checked by reading source: readme-tags.test.js:85 genuinely derives via countTagsInCorpus() (DERIVED, correct); select.test.js:9 is a literal 40 about corpus data not a document (BORDERLINE, correct).

items.title: Build the detection floor: bounded, rule-generated mutation matrix with an identity control, baselined at 20b7ede
items.acceptance: tools/mutation-matrix.mjs exists, is zero-dependency, is NOT collected by the suite's own file glob, and adds zero tests. It states its generation rule in the file itself and enumerates at most 30 mutations produced by that rule — exactly one falsifying mutation per machine-checked document claim the W-1 inventory found — plus exactly ONE identity (no-op) mutation as converse control. For each mutation it applies the edit to a scratch copy, runs the suite there, records which NAMED guards fired, and leaves the working tree byte-identical. The identity control must leave the suite green; a mutation no guard catches is reported as SILENT, never omitted. Any claim the generation rule produces but the harness skips is listed with its reason. The baseline result against 20b7ede is recorded in tools/mutation-matrix-baseline.json in a machine-comparable shape.
items.notes: Risk: ~30 suite runs. The suite spawns the real binary (cli/pipe tests) and shells out to git (node-support-citation), so the scratch copy must be a real git work tree or those two guards skip/fail for ENVIRONMENTAL reasons rather than because of the mutation — which would corrupt the matrix. Decide and STATE how the scratch copy handles git (clone vs worktree vs accept skips and mark N/A). Baseline at 20b7ede per S-1; HEAD 912a2a4 changed only .swarm/, so src/bin/test should be identical — confirm, do not assume.
items.verify_note: Conductor gate: independent control proved the suite is discriminating (a neutral README edit leaves it GREEN), plus two hand-replicated mutations each firing exactly the named guard. Mutation count 18 == W-1 inventory INCLUDED count 18, +1 identity = 19, under the 30 cap. Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-003-verify-W-2.txt

items.title: Count the citation two-commit tax over repo history, as a rerunnable tool that changes nothing
items.acceptance: tools/citation-tax.mjs walks committed history and derives, without hardcoding the answer: (a) how many commits touched the cited pathspec src/ bin/ test/ .github; (b) of those, how many landed while the citation guard existed and therefore made the README's cited diff non-empty at that commit — knowingly committed RED; (c) how many separate follow-up commits were spent re-citing; (d) the commit gap between each breakage and its repair, so same-commit and later-cycle repairs are distinguishable. It prints the exact derivation per event (breaking SHA, repairing SHA, gap) and ends with a plain recommendation on whether the ritual is intrinsic to a self-falsifying claim or an artifact of an over-claiming pathspec. It changes no pathspec, no assertion, no citation.
items.notes: PLAN's starting measurements, to be RE-DERIVED not trusted: 48 of 255 commits touch the pathspec across all history, but the guard only came into existence at 5f833ab, so 'every commit in history' is the wrong denominator and would inflate the tax. Honest denominator looks like the 6 pathspec-touching commits from 5f833ab forward (5f833ab, c08562b, c9dd7ff, 2b003ea, 4b63e91, 22fdeac→a302f71→7e50d6f), each of which appears to have cost a re-citation commit — i.e. ~100%. The guard also CHANGED SHAPE mid-history (c08562b made it fail loud on ambiguity; 2b003ea added the working-tree comparison), so 'would have turned red' is only well-defined against the guard version live at that commit — decide and state the convention. [CYCLE 2 VERIFIED] Conductor gate: tool exits 0, 320 lines, wrote nothing (tree byte-identical across a run, only the conductors own evidence files appeared). No event SHA, tax figure or denominator appears as a literal in the source; no mutating git verb in the source. Denominator RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY by the conductor: git rev-list --first-parent --count 5f833ab~1..HEAD -- src bin test .github = 6, out of 39 first-parent commits in the window - exactly the tools 6 SHAs, including its correction that 7e50d6f touches nothing in the pathspec and that 22fdeac/a302f71 is one event billed once. Event 3 hand-checked end to end: README at c9dd7ff cited base c08562b; git diff c08562b..c9dd7ff -- src bin test .github names .github/workflows/test.yml (non-empty -> RED); repair 6c0c298 re-cited the base to c9dd7ff; gap = 2. Every cell matches.

items.title: Close KI-R6-3: consolidate the two guards reading the same 'Tags on exactly one entry' row, or publish the mutation that separates them
items.acceptance: The mutation falsifying README's 'Tags on exactly one entry' counts-table row is run through the detection floor and the set of NAMED guards it fires is recorded. If the two guards' firing sets are identical, exactly ONE is removed, and re-running the matrix shows every mutation detected at the 20b7ede baseline is still detected and the identity control still green. If the firing sets DIFFER, both are kept and the distinguishing mutation — the specific edit one catches and the other does not — is recorded in the test file naming what each guard uniquely catches. Either outcome closes it; 'keep both because removing one feels risky' does not. A drop in test count is a PASS.
items.notes: The two guards are in test/readme-tags.test.js: the test at ~line 434 (Q-4's structural replacement) and the second assertion inside the test at ~line 1598. The file's own comment block at lines 150-162 already concedes they are redundant in the strict sense — 'a wrong value in that row fails both and no mutation fails only one of them' — so consolidation is the likely branch. NOTE removing the ~1598 assertion would also drop the 'Tags on 2 or more entries' check, so target ~434 or be surgical. BIGGEST RISK IN THE PLAN: this is the ONLY item touching test/, inside the cited pathspec, so the commit that lands it makes the README's cited diff non-empty and turns both citation guards RED on a full clone. Closing the window needs a NEW Actions run id, which needs a successful push AND Actions API access — unverified from this environment (origin is https and master is level with origin/master, encouraging but not proof). Sequence LAST among code-touching items, GATE on a confirmed ability to obtain a run id, and predict the window in the commit message per S-8. There is no test/-free path to the removal branch. [CYCLE 4 DONE] CONSOLIDATE branch, forced by measurement not preference. Builder probed 9 falsifications of the "Tags on exactly one entry" row; firing sets identical on all of them, differing in exactly ONE direction (falsifying "Tags on 2 or more entries" fires the ~1598 guard alone). No edit fires ~434 without also firing ~1598, so ~434 is a strict subset and is the determined removal. Attribution controls: ~434 deleted -> still caught; ~1598 deleted -> still caught; BOTH deleted -> SILENT. Test count 129 -> 128. Conductor gate 6/6 on two throwaway clones (detection preserved via the survivor; converse control green; window measured in both uncommitted and committed states; branch read off the diff, not the claim). Gate cell C1 initially failed on the CONDUCTOR's own porcelain parser (.trim() before split ate the first line's status column) — corrected in runs/gate-c4-w7-c1-addendum.mjs and recorded as D-R8-10, not silently re-run.

RULING W8-R1, printed on every run including failing ones: a mutation SKIPPED at HEAD because its anchor occurs 0 times is NOT detection lost -- it is a RETIRED CLAIM in its own always-listed bucket -- with the case AGAINST recorded (anchor-count-0 is a mechanical proxy; a REWORDED claim would evade it), the falsifier named (guard-inventory.mjs at HEAD is the adjudicator for reworded-but-unguarded claims), and a scope guard failing any skip whose reason is not anchor-count-0 as SKIP-UNPROVEN. Partition at HEAD: 14 same-guard, 1 guard-changed (M08, named on both sides), 3 claim-gone (M01-M03), 0 detection lost. Conductor gate 13/13: C3 RE-DERIVED the artifact independently (own --rev HEAD --json run, 0 verdict differences, 0 guardTitle differences, identical skippedClaims, identity control GREEN both sides) so the artifact is not fabricated; C4' recomputed the whole partition from firedGuards and required set-for-set agreement; C5/C5b are conductor injections on ids the builder did not use (M09 CAUGHT->SILENT, M15 deleted from both arrays), both correctly failed and named; C6 is the green control on the same path; C7 proved the FRESH-BY-CONTENT exemption cannot wave through a genuinely stale record (measuredCommit -> e40736c, whose diff touches tools/mutation-matrix.mjs: exit 3 STALE, no partition printed). items.title: One entry point that re-runs every published finding, so S-6 is checkable rather than asserted

If the mutation matrix is slow (~30 suite runs), give it an opt-out flag and state in the file what the default excludes. Conductor gate 6/6, including the discriminator that matters: replacing tools/citation-tax.mjs with a bare throw in a scratch clone makes the roll-up say PROBLEM, and the same clone unbroken says clean. items.title: Seven CLI behaviours are unspecified and a human should rule on them (from J-6 + N-4 + D-44 + Q-7 + TS-5)
items.acceptance: A human rules on SEVEN behaviours the Domain rules do not currently decide (two enumerated inline below; five more — D-42, D-43, D-44, D-45, D-46 — enumerated in the notes and written up in SPEC.md § Undecided behaviours), and the ruling is written into SPEC.md as an explicit clause either way. (1) --help vs usage-error precedence when both appear in argv: the shipped behaviour is that the usage error WINS in both argv orders (measured: `--help --seed abc` and `--seed abc --help` both exit 2 with "aphorism: flag --seed requires a numeric value" on stderr). (2) Whether `--seed -0` and `--seed 0` are THE SAME SEED: they are `===` in JavaScript, but toUint32Seed folds the IEEE-754 bit pattern including the sign bit, so they select DIFFERENT aphorisms (measured: seed 0 -> Kernighan "most effective debugging tool"; seed -0 -> Saint-Exupery "Perfection is achieved"). Either behaviour is defensible; the SPEC decides neither.
items.notes:
FILED AT CYCLE 4 from J-6, which measured both and correctly declined to pin either with a test. This is a SPEC decision, not a swarm task, and it is filed the way T-040 is: a human ratifies or reverses, and the item is not dispatchable until they do.

WHY NO TEST WAS ADDED, and why that was right: the Domain rules resolve exactly ONE flag-vs-error precedence question explicitly — for --list ("A seed that fails to parse is still a usage error under --list"). The existence of that carve-out is evidence the author does not treat "usage-error trumps other flags" as self-evidently general; where they meant it to generalise, they said so. They never said it for --help. An assertion pinning today s behaviour would therefore be a future false rejection rather than coverage — which is the failure mode J-6 exists to avoid. Same logic for -0/0: the rule guarantees determinism PER SEED VALUE and says nothing about whether -0 and 0 are one value or two.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER RULES ON (2): if the answer is "they are the same seed", that is a PRODUCT bug in toUint32Seed and closing it is a src/ change, which this run s non-goals fence off. If the answer is "they are distinguishable bit patterns, by design", the fix is one SPEC sentence and nothing else. The cheap ruling and the expensive one are not symmetric, so rule before anyone writes code.

HONEST NOTE ON (1) FROM THE BUILDER, disclosed before any gate looked: its "does not map" call on case 1 rests on an INFERENCE from the --list carve-out (silence implies deliberate scoping) rather than on direct textual statement. A reasonable reviewer could read the Exit-codes clause as unconditional and call the current behaviour a hole rather than an unspecified choice. The disagreement is recorded rather than resolved. | CYCLE 4: N-4 added TWO more rulings to this item, both measured. (3) REPEATED --tag/--author (D-42): shipped behaviour is last-occurrence-wins and it is UNPROTECTED - conductor reproduced it independently (--tag humor --tag design --list prints the 14-entry design list; a first-wins mutant prints the 9-entry humor list; the suite stays 102p/0f on both). SPEC spells every filter flag in the singular and never mentions repetition, so last-wins is an artifact of assignment order in parseArgs, not a contract. (4) EMPTY/WHITESPACE --seed (D-43): SPEC Selection says --seed accepts any value that Number() parses to a non-NaN number, and Number("")===0 is non-NaN, so the literal reading says ACCEPT; the implementation rejects with exit 2 and SPEC Exit-codes calls a missing flag argument bad usage. The two clauses point opposite ways, so there is no decided behaviour to test against - a human must pick one.

Independent re-derivation raises confidence that this gap is real and human-owned, and it cost nothing to learn because the agent was not told the answer. NEW FACT for whoever rules, which D-43 does NOT record: the refusal is specific to EMPTY and WHITESPACE-ONLY values. Whitespace-PADDED values are ACCEPTED today — `node bin/aphorism.js --seed " 5 " --json` is byte-identical to `--seed 5` and exits 0 (conductor-measured, cycle 6, .swarm/runs/cycle-006-qa-verify.txt). So the implementation is not uniformly "trim then reject"; src/args.js:55 rejects only when the trimmed value is empty, then hands the UNTRIMMED string to Number(), which itself tolerates padding. A ruling of "accept per Number()" is therefore a smaller change than it looks: it deletes one guard clause rather than reworking seed parsing.

|| CYCLE 13, RUN #3 review-fix pass: a FIFTH ruling joins this item. (5) EMPTY FLAG VALUE, '=' FORM vs SPACE FORM (D-44). items.title: P-5 (green at every commit) and P-6 (the self-falsifying citation guard) are in direct conflict, and only a human can rule on which gives
items.acceptance: A human rules on ONE of: (a) P-5 wording is amended to exempt the single commit that introduces a src/bin/test/.github change from the full-clone green requirement, on the stated ground that the CI run which refreshes the citation cannot exist before the push; (b) the citation design changes so the window closes; or (c) the guard is retired. Until then the exception stands recorded, never re-labelled as a pass.
items.notes: MEASURED cycle 5, not inferred. P-6 mechanizes README Node-support own falsifier. Because the pathspec it cites is `src bin test .github`, ANY commit touching those paths makes the cited diff non-empty at that commit, so the suite is RED on a full clone until a follow-up commit re-cites to a CI run for it — and that CI run cannot exist until after the push. Commit 5f833ab is exactly that case: red on a full clone, green in CI (the guard skips on depth-1 checkout), repaired by c0337f1. P-5 requires green at >=119 on EVERY commit this run makes, so 5f833ab is a genuine exception and is recorded as one in .swarm/runs/cycle-005-verify-P-6.txt. WHY THIS IS HUMAN-OWNED: every available disposition edits a locked SPEC must-have or deletes a shipped claim, and this run non-goals forbid the swarm doing either for itself. Note the window is not a defect in the test — it is the price of the claim being checkable at all, and the alternative (a citation nothing runs) is the state that let the claim go stale undetected two cycles ago. | cycle 10 SHARPENED THE CONFLICT WITHOUT RESOLVING IT. RF-5 made the guard fire on the WORKING TREE, so the exception is no longer discovered a cycle late by a full clone — it is now visible pre-commit, to the very run that causes it. That is strictly better for detection and it changes nothing about the disposition: the window between push and re-citation still exists and still violates "green at every commit", because CI cannot describe a commit that has not been pushed. Ruling (a)/(b)/(c) is still a human call, and it is now a call a human will meet on EVERY commit touching src/bin/test/.github rather than occasionally. | carried into improvement run #6 unchanged; the brief forbids the ruling this needs

The three existing directions (README-side, doc-side, honest control) must all still behave as they do today, demonstrated by real runs.
items.notes: Found by the cycle-3 conductor gate, BEYOND the P-1 acceptance clause. Measured: git rev-parse --show-toplevel from a nested checkout with .git deleted returns /opt/targets/aphorism-cli (the PARENT repo), so `git show HEAD:README.md` silently resolves against an ancestor. In the gate the ancestor happened to be the same project, so the attribution looked correct - that coincidence is exactly what makes it worth fixing. Run genuinely outside any repo the fallback DOES fire correctly (verified), so this is narrow: only the nested-inside-unrelated-repo case. Low severity; the failure mode is a confidently-stated attribution that could name the wrong side. [CYCLE 6 DONE] Builder added resolvedToplevelIsOwnRoot(): `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from rootDir, realpath-compared to rootDir; readHeadBlob() returns null when they differ, routing to the pre-existing honest undetermined-direction message. Conductor gate: C8' rebuilt the nested-non-repo scenario independently, confirmed `--show-toplevel` still resolves to the ANCESTOR /opt/targets/aphorism-cli, and showed the tool no longer asserts 'own git HEAD version' and instead takes the undetermined path. C9' is the converse control in a clone that IS its own toplevel: the tool still names README as the side that moved AND still names the git anchor, so the fix is narrow rather than a blanket degrade. C10 is the honest control on the live tree (exit 0, OK). NOTE: the first-pass cells C8/C9 FAILED because the conductor's perturbation rewrote the '### Node support' HEADING, which the tool matches exactly, short-circuiting at the no-section branch before any attribution ran - a gate defect, not a defect in this work. See D-R8-17.

items.title: Close the citation window opened by W-7: re-cite README's Node-support matrix at the new run id

Scope was the whole risk — touching anything under src/ bin/ test/ .github/ would have RE-OPENED the very window it closes. Structurally unlike the previous move: this time the commit that changed the paths WAS the head of its push, so it has a run of its own.

items.title: tools/mutation-matrix.mjs cannot measure any tree but 20b7ede, so W-8 is unsatisfiable as shipped
items.acceptance:
tools/mutation-matrix.mjs can measure a caller-named tree.
A. Invoked with NO arguments it still measures 20b7ede and its emitted matrix is
   verdict-for-verdict identical to tools/mutation-matrix-baseline.json. The default
   path is a frozen contract: tools/run-all.mjs invokes it with zero cliArgs, and the
   committed baseline JSON is the comparison W-8 depends on.
B. Invoked so as to name a different tree, it demonstrably measures THAT tree — the run
   must state the resolved full sha of what it measured, and that sha must equal the
   named rev resolved independently.
C. A mutation whose transcribed guardTitle no longer exists in the measured tree must
   NOT abort the run. W-7 consolidated two same-row guards into one, so this case is
   live at HEAD, not hypothetical. The CAUGHT/SILENT verdict is what S-1 turns on;
   attribution to a named guard is secondary and must degrade to an explicitly recorded
   state rather than throwing.
items.notes: Line 89 as shipped: const BASELINE = '20b7ede', with a detached checkout at it near line 482. D-R8-12: as shipped, W-8 "re-run the matrix at final HEAD" would measure the baseline TWICE and return a guaranteed-identical matrix — which W-8's own clause anticipates as a legitimate null result. The two outcomes are observationally identical, so a builder could discharge W-8 honestly and be wrong. Do not change WHAT the mutation set is; only what tree it is measured against.

items.title: tools/mutation-matrix.mjs uses a shared scratch path, so two concurrent runs clobber each other
items.acceptance:
Two concurrent invocations of tools/mutation-matrix.mjs no longer clobber one another.
The scratch tree must not be a fixed path shared by every invocation — as shipped,
SCRATCH_ROOT is ROOT/.scratch-W-2 at line 87.
Required proof is a DEMONSTRATION, not an inspection: two invocations running at
genuinely overlapping times, both completing, neither reporting a git error caused by
the other's cleanup. The pre-fix code must be shown failing that same way, for contrast —
a fix with no reproduced baseline failure is unattributable.
Whatever path scheme replaces it must still be fully removed on exit (the finally block
near line 604) and must never survive into a commit.
items.notes: Observed, not inferred: during cycle 4, W-9's run-all.mjs ran the matrix while W-7's builder invoked it too; the second run deleted and recreated the clone under the first, which died with spawnSync git ENOENT inside resetClone near line 495. Both agents reported it independently. W-9 shipping a dispatcher that runs the matrix makes concurrent invocation MORE likely from here, not less.

items.title: mutation-matrix.mjs can emit machine-readable JSON only for the default rev, so W-8 has no structured side to compare at HEAD
items.acceptance: A matrix run against a non-default rev can produce the same structured record the default run writes, WITHOUT being able to overwrite tools/mutation-matrix-baseline.json. The existing refusal of `--rev` together with `--write-baseline` must stay in force — that guard is correct and is not what this item relaxes; the committed baseline must remain writable only from the default rev. Proof: a HEAD run emits a record that can be diffed row-by-row against the committed baseline by a caller, and the committed baseline file is byte-unmoved by that run.
items.notes: Found by the cycle-5 gate, not by the builder. W-8 must prove "no mutation detected at baseline goes undetected at final HEAD". At HEAD the tool prints that verdict only as TEXT: --write-baseline is refused whenever --rev is given (correctly, since it would corrupt the instrument), and there is no other structured output path. So W-8 would have to compare a committed JSON against scraped prose — precisely the "never assert against prose matched by regex" failure the playbook warns about. The cycle-5 gate hit this directly: it could compare the DEFAULT run verdict-for-verdict against the JSON, but had to fall back to tool-owned text lines for the HEAD run. [CYCLE 6 DONE] Builder added a `--json` flag that routes the human report to stderr and prints the SAME `baseline` record --write-baseline persists, to stdout. Conductor gate: C3 proved the zero-arg contract byte-identical to the pre-change HEAD tool (both run, stdout diffed); C4 parsed the ENTIRE --rev HEAD --json stdout as one JSON document and diffed it row-by-row by id against the committed baseline (18 committed rows, 15 at HEAD, 15 shared, 0 verdict differences, M01-M03 listed explicitly as baseline-only rather than folded into a pass); C5 is the converse control (zero-arg stdout does NOT parse as JSON, so the flag is not a no-op); C6 showed --rev+--write-baseline still refused with exit 2, and also refused with --json added, so --json is not a back door to the committed file; C7 showed the baseline sha256 unmoved across every run. C2' confirmed structurally that `baseline` is declared at top level (L774) before both the write branch (L791) and the emit block (L804), so --json cannot be a latent ReferenceError.
